question: Does the methodology choose better which biological information to use for predicting enzyme activity?

positive_control.what_this_proves: when a sparse subset really carries the signal, this harness finds most of it and selection beats using everything. A null on real data is therefore about the data, not the instrument.

what_this_is_not.a_shap_value_is_not_evidence_of_value: it is an attribution inside one fitted model. Two collinear probes split one signal and both look weak; a feature the model leaned on can be useless out of sample. SHAP proposes an ordering here and never settles a claim.
what_this_is_not.the_curve_is_not_a_validated_panel_size: the k at the curve's best point was chosen with hindsight across the whole grid. The validated size is the one the inner folds chose, reported separately, and the two often differ.
what_this_is_not.beating_a_selector_is_not_predicting_pha: every endpoint here is an in-vitro activity or a functional screen score. Nothing in this module touches a clearance, an AUC or a concentration.
what_this_is_not.a_selector_cannot_abstain_by_accident: hand any of these pure noise and it returns the k luckiest columns. That is why the permuted-outcome control is run beside every real result rather than on request.
what_this_is_not.agreement_between_selectors_is_not_truth: two selectors can agree because they share a bias. Agreement is reported as a stability diagnostic, never as confirmation.
